solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Traditional Cluedo weapon nicked straight from the kitchen?

parts.note: the lead piping is one of the original weapons in the board game Cluedo (Clue in the US); the last word of its name is used
British slang: nicked means stolen, and stolen goods are hot

explanation.surface: Someone has pinched the old lead piping from the Cluedo box, carrying it straight out of the kitchen, one of the game's rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen is a Cluedo room, which makes the surface feel like a game scene; it is really the definition, about food served at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Food served very hot, freshly cooked, has come straight from the stove to the table.

clue.text: Chronicler looks briefly for an audience

indicators.note: something said for listeners is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: to peep is to take a quick look; the third-person form fits looks

explanation.surface: A diarist casts quick glances towards the people watching him.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Pepys kept the famous diary of 1660s London; his name is pronounced like the word for quick looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepys is the best-known English diarist, a recorder of daily events, hence a chronicler.

clue.text: Entertaining creatures out of place in Metamorphoses

indicators.note: letters out of place have been moved from their proper positions, so the fodder is rearranged

explanation.surface: Amusing animals turn up oddly in Ovid's Metamorphoses, a poem about transformations.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime horse is two actors in one horse costume, a staple of British Christmas pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: The costumed two-person horses of pantomime are comic stage animals, designed purely to amuse an audience.

clue.text: Number one gundog polishing off last piece of meat …

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: to polish off something is to finish or dispose of it, so the dog's final letter is removed

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog used by hunters to find game

explanation.surface: The top gundog wolfs down the final scrap of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue into the next one; it has no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisette is a small round boneless cut, typically of lamb, so a portion of meat.

clue.text: … eats hot chop in little bits

parts.note: to have a meal is to eat it, so has stands for eats

explanation.surface: Carrying on from the previous clue, the dog eats a hot chop cut small.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening ellipsis joins the dog of the clue before; chop is a verb in the definition, not the cut of meat it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To hash food is to cut it up finely, as in making a hash of meat and potato.

clue.text: Fluid daft nurses fed in intravenously

indicators.note: something fluid has no fixed shape, so these letters flow into a new order

explanation.surface: Careless nurses give a patient liquid through a drip.
explanation.walkthrough: Fluid looks like the noun for what is dripped in, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A transfusion puts blood or another liquid straight into a vein, which is what intravenous means.

clue.text: Search far end of Yorkshire dale

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

indicators.note: the far end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of the county name is taken

explanation.surface: Hunting through the remotest corner of a Yorkshire valley.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire is a county in northern England famed for its dales, which makes the place feel like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A combe is a short steep valley, especially in southern England, so it is a synonym for a dale.

clue.text: Gangland boss better operating close to home

parts.note: to cap something is to outdo or better it
a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A mob leader is doing better now he runs his business near where he lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Better is a verb here, not the adjective it looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone ran organised crime in Prohibition-era Chicago, the archetypal gangster chief.

clue.text: One carving, with inscription, impressive Madonna and child

parts.note: monumental means great in scale or importance
the Madonna is the Virgin Mary, the mother of Christ; ma is an informal word for mother
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A sculptor carving a grand Madonna and Child, with words cut into the base.
explanation.walkthrough: Madonna and child calls up a religious statue; here it is just mother plus son.
explanation.definitionFit: A monumental mason is a stonemason who makes gravestones and memorials, cutting lettering into them.

clue.text: Lustful old boy returns inside, chasing queen's messenger

indicators.note: something chasing comes behind, so the rest follows the queen

parts.note: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen; the 's is taken as is

indicators.note: the reversed former pupil is placed within the lustful word

parts.note: randy is British slang for sexually eager

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it went, so read it backwards

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for a former pupil of a school

explanation.surface: A randy former schoolboy is back behind bars, running after the Queen's courier.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen's messenger is a real job title, a diplomatic courier, so the solver reads it as one phrase; only the second word defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand boy is a lad employed to run errands and deliver messages, a junior messenger.

clue.text: Stationery item — probably not much point going into it

definitions.text: Stationery item — probably not much point going into it

parts.words: probably not much point going into it
parts.note: reads as a shrug that the effort is pointless; really a blunt pencil, with little point on its tip, being pushed into the device

explanation.surface: A wry aside that it is hardly worth bothering with some office supply.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun is on point: a pencil that goes in has a blunt tip, so it has not much point.
explanation.definitionFit: The device restores a sharp tip to a blunted pencil, a desk item sold with stationery.

clue.text: Drab partners holding hands, having nothing to hide

indicators.note: the partners have, or keep, the nothing within them
something hidden is covered up, so it sits concealed between the two partners

parts.note: in bridge, North and South are partners, each holding a hand of cards
love is zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A dull couple walk hand in hand, with nothing to conceal.
explanation.walkthrough: Drab is a noun here: an old word for a slovenly woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloven is an untidy, careless person, and drab is an old word for a slattern of that kind.

clue.text: Unanimously answer child, returning call

parts.note: a son is a child

indicators.note: something returning goes back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: A parent replies to a child who is shouting back.
explanation.walkthrough: A for answer is the abbreviation used in quiz books and exams.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as one man is an idiom meaning all together, with every person in agreement.

clue.text: Mercenary lover puts one off holding dance

indicators.note: the shortened word holds the dance within it
the one is put out of the word, so that letter is dropped
off means away or removed, completing the instruction to take the letter out

parts.note: a fancier is someone devoted to something, such as a pigeon fancier
the Roman numeral for one
a reel is a lively Scottish folk dance

explanation.surface: A mercenary's sweetheart dumps someone at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The medieval free lance was a knight who sold his services to any lord, hence the modern word.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelancer works for whoever pays, as a hired soldier does, the word's original sense.

clue.text: Rowdy old Tories scrambled aboard coach

indicators.note: passengers aboard are inside the vehicle, so these letters go within it

parts.note: a coach is a long-distance bus

indicators.note: scrambled things are mixed up, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Elderly Conservatives clamber on to a coach, making a din.
explanation.walkthrough: Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Boisterous means noisy, energetic and unruly, a close synonym of rowdy.

clue.text: Children's dog houses in display initially — placed here?

indicators.note: a house holds people within it, so the dog word contains the rest

parts.note: bow-wow is a child's word for a dog
taken as written

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of this word is used

explanation.surface: A child's toy dog is put out on show, perhaps in a shop front.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue's own display: shops place goods on show in such a curved window.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow window is a curved bay window, often where shopkeepers set out items on show.

clue.text: Commission from East shunned by upper-class prig

indicators.note: something shunned is avoided, so the letter is left out
in an across clue, coming from the east means reading from right to left

parts.note: a bonus is an extra payment, like a commission on sales
U is the old label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A posh prig turns down a commission from an eastern client.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were labels popularised in 1950s Britain for upper-class and other speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A snob looks down on those of lower status, and a prig is a self-righteous person who does likewise.

clue.text: Article seized by master from kid, perhaps

indicators.note: something seized is held tight, so it sits inside the other word

parts.note: to master a skill is to learn it
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster confiscates an item from a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: Kid looks like a child, but it is soft leather made from young goatskin.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathern means made of leather, and kid is one example, as perhaps signals.

clue.text: Small, soft lament

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
p, for piano, is the musical direction to play softly

explanation.surface: A little, quiet cry of grief.
explanation.definitionFit: To weep is to shed tears in sorrow, and to lament is to mourn aloud in the same way.

clue.text: Worsening classes during last month ultimately rally

indicators.note: the classes are placed within the month

parts.note: December is the last month of the year; Dec is its abbreviation
genera, plural of genus, are classes in biology

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter

parts.note: only the closing letter of this word is used

explanation.surface: School classes go downhill through December before finally picking up.
explanation.definitionFit: Degeneracy is the state of decline, a deterioration from a former quality, hence a worsening.

clue.text: Small vehicle accommodating a large quantity

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so the car holds the next letters

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A little car fits in a big load.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads a large quantity as one phrase; quantity alone defines, in the mathematical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a scalar is a quantity with magnitude but no direction, unlike a vector.

clue.text: Warship crew's heading in to press youngster

indicators.note: the crew's first letter goes into the other pieces

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
a lad is a boy

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of this word is used

explanation.surface: A ship's crew heads in to press-gang a young lad into service.
explanation.walkthrough: Press-gangs once forced young men into naval service, which makes press look like the navy's word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ironclad was a 19th-century steam warship protected by iron armour plates.

clue.text: Visible evidence of logging puzzles

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... of trees left when timber is cut
second meaning: to stump someone is to baffle them

explanation.walkthrough: Logging looks like recording data, but it is felling trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Tree stumps remain after felling, and to stump a person is to perplex them with a question.

clue.text: Divine judgment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to ... is to detect or intuit, as to divine is
second meaning: good ... is sound judgment

explanation.walkthrough: Divine judgment reads as God's verdict; divine is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To sense is to perceive intuitively, and common sense is practical wisdom or sound reasoning.

clue.text: Day in Rome that is timeless

indicators.note: less means without, so time, t, is removed

parts.note: id est is Latin for that is, abbreviated ie

explanation.surface: A day in the Eternal City that never ends.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the Ides fell mid-month, the 15th or 13th, a fixed date for counting days.

clue.text: Doctor Crippen loses dad, being forced to leave home

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered

explanation.surface: Dr Crippen, the Edwardian murderer, loses his father and is driven from his house.
explanation.walkthrough: Hawley Crippen was a notorious 1910 London murderer always called Dr Crippen, so Doctor looks like his title.
explanation.definitionFit: A displaced person is a refugee, someone made to leave their own country or home.

clue.text: More prudent wife is heard not seen oddly

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the odd letters are not seen, so only the even ones are kept

parts.note: its second and fourth letters are kept, the odd ones dropped

explanation.surface: An old saying that a sensible wife should be heard but not seen, twisted strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the proverb that children should be seen and not heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiser is the comparative of wise, having better judgment, so it means showing more prudence.

clue.text: Ringing area in on-screen shot

indicators.note: the area letter sits within the rearranged word
shot means broken or ruined, so the letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: A ringing noise in a part of a film shot on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Resonance is a prolonged sound produced by vibration, like the reverberation of a bell.
